caption: The drawing depicts a single wooden chair positioned at a slight angle, showing both the seat and the backrest. The chair is constructed from medium brown wood and features a simple, rustic design. The seat is flat with visible wood grain and is secured to four sturdy, slightly tapered legs connected by horizontal supports for stability. The backrest is tall and angled, consisting of two vertical side rails with rounded ends that extend above the topmost horizontal back slat. The backrest includes two wide, rectangular slats, each decorated with carved or incised patterns of horizontal and diagonal lines. The front panel of the seat and the lower part of the backrest share similar decorative incisions. The composition is rendered with realistic shading and perspective, and the background is plain and off-white. In the lower right corner, there is a small handwritten note in green that reads, "Motel G. Claflin Taos, N. Mexico."
title: Wooden Chair
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
